chunks: Muhammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from Dāwūd ibn Zurbī, who said:

I said to Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام: I deal with some people, and sometimes they send to me and take from me a bondwoman and an animal, and they go away with it from me. Then some wealth belonging to them comes into my possession, so I take from it an amount equal to what they took from me.
So he عليه السلام said: Take from them an amount equal to what they took from you, and do not add to it.

key_terms.أُعَامِلُ: I engage in dealings or transactions
key_terms.الْجَارِيَةَ: a bondwoman or female slave taken as property
key_terms.بِقَدْرِ: to the measure of; equal to the exact amount
key_terms.لَا تَزِدْ: do not exceed or take more than is due

ai.seo_question: Can a person recover the value of property wrongfully taken from him by taking an equivalent amount from the other party’s wealth?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about recovering one’s property or its equivalent when others have wrongfully taken it and their wealth later comes into one’s possession. The Imam عليه السلام permits taking only the exact equivalent of the loss and forbids exceeding that amount, emphasizing justice and restraint.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3703 - Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Dawud ibn Zurbi who said:

I said to Abu Al-Hasan (as), "I deal with some people, and sometimes they send to me and take a bondwoman or an animal from me, and they take it away. Then their wealth later comes into my possession. Can I take from it an amount equivalent to what they took from me?"
Imam (as) said: "Take from them an amount equal to what they took from you and do not take more than that."
